To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

NK cells can be divided into 3 subsets according to the level of CD 8 expression, and that sHLA-I can induce apoptosis in CD8(bright)-positive NK cell clones, which is inhibited by members of the NK receptor superfamily.
soluble HLA-I molecules induce natural killer (NK)-cell apoptosis through the engagement with their receptor CD8.
the CD8 molecule can be divided into three subgroups and that the level of CD 8 expression is a key determinant of the susceptibility to apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of NK cell apoptosis induced by sHLA-I, which may be of importance for the regulation of NK cell homeostasis and the pathogenesis of NK cell-associated diseases.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of NK cell function by HLA-I molecules.
the identification of a new pathway of NK cell apoptosis that involves the interaction between sHLAs and CD8, the engagement of Fas/Fas-L, and the down-regulatory effect of inhibitory receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soluble HLA-I molecules can induce NK cell apoptosis by triggering CD8 molecules and that this apoptotic signal is down-modulated by inhibitory receptors superfamily.
CD8 is a receptor for sHLA-I, that CD8 expression level determines the magnitude of the apoptotic signal, and that the Fas pathway is involved in this process.

soluble HLA class molecules induce NK cell apoptosis through the interaction with CD4, CD8, and Fas/Fas ligand pathway, and that the level of CD4 and CD8 expression on the cell surface is a key factor for the susceptibility to sHLA-I.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

soluble HLA class-I molecules induce natural killer (NK)-cell apoptosis through the engagement with CD8: evidence that a negative regulation exert by members of the inhibitor receptor superfamily is exerted.
sHLA-I molecules induce NK cell apoptosis by triggering CD8 and Fas/Fas ligand pathway.
soluble HLA class 1 induces natural killer cell apoptosis by engaging CD8 and that this process is negatively regulated by the members of the inhibiting receptor superfamily.

NK cell apoptosis is triggered by soluble HLA-I molecules via the engagement of CD 8.
NK cells are able to sense the presence of sHLA-I in the microenvironment and to react by undergoing apoptosis.
